evidence_class: Public narratives that motivate abstract local simulator perturbations. They supply no numeric coefficients, labels or telemetry. Mechanism-to-source assignment is researcher judgment.
inherits: docs/research/incident_dynamics_sources_v1.json (eight v1 sources remain attached to constant_pressure in v2 and to the paper population)
verification: Each URL was fetched by a research subagent; all 24 were re-checked on 2026-10-18 (19 HTTP 200; SEC, CISA and Medium return 403 to scripted clients and two CISA advisories were confirmed with a separate fetcher).

generic_mechanisms.physical/vibration_degradation: Generic wear family; no specific incident source is claimed.

holdout_rule: Sources motivating held-out mechanisms are disjoint from development-mechanism sources; held-out families are generated only for the registered final catalog.

sources.title: External Technical Root Cause Analysis – Channel File 291
sources.mechanism: A content update defined 21 input fields but the sensor code only supplied 20 values to match against; when a later instance first exercised the 21st field, the kernel-mode interpreter read past the end of its input array and faulted. Because the faulting component runs in the boot path, affected Windows hosts entered a crash/reboot loop en masse.
sources.state_mapping: process_count (dim 0) collapses to near zero as the host faults and bootloops; abstractly a fault flag firing on a single malformed configuration event.
sources.caveats: Vendor self-report; gives field-count and bounds-check root cause but no per-host time-series telemetry of the crash dynamics.
sources.verification: Fetched PDF; extracted text with pypdf, cover page reads 'Page 1 of 12 2024-08-06' and section 'External Technical Root Cause Analysis – Channel File 291'.

sources.title: More details about the October 4 outage
sources.mechanism: A maintenance command intended to assess backbone capacity instead withdrew all backbone connectivity, and an audit tool that should have rejected it had a bug. With the backbone gone, DNS servers judged themselves unhealthy and withdrew their route advertisements, so dependent services became globally unreachable in a self-reinforcing chain.
sources.state_mapping: process_count (dim 0) and heap_fraction (dim 1) as proxies for dependent-service availability collapsing in sequence once an upstream resource is removed.
sources.caveats: Network/control-plane incident; mapping onto single-host OS variables is analogical. No numeric telemetry published.
sources.verification: Fetched page; confirmed title, author Santosh Janardhan, date Oct 5 2021.

sources.title: Postmortem of database outage of January 31
sources.mechanism: A load spike made a replica fall behind until its logs were unrecoverable; during manual recovery an engineer deleted the live primary's data directory (~300 GB) instead of the replica's, and silent backup failures meant most restore paths were gone.
sources.state_mapping: fs_file_count (dim 2) and disk_usage (dim 3) drop as a step when the data directory is wiped; preceding replication lag is a slow monotone divergence.
sources.caveats: Narrative postmortem; replication-lag growth is described qualitatively, not as logged time series.
sources.verification: Fetched page; confirmed title, publisher, Feb 10 2017 date and the deletion/replication/backup chain.

sources.title: Summary of the Amazon S3 Service Disruption in the Northern Virginia (US-EAST-1) Region
sources.mechanism: A capacity-management command was entered with a wrong parameter and removed far more servers than intended, including nodes serving the S3 index and placement subsystems; both had to fully restart, and the restart plus integrity checks took longer than expected, so requests failed during the rebuild.
sources.state_mapping: process_count (dim 0) steps down as capacity is removed, then heap_fraction (dim 1) spikes during the full restart/rebuild before recovery.
sources.caveats: Event-date dated; no quantitative restart-time curves given.
sources.verification: Fetched page; confirmed title and that a mistyped command removed more servers than intended, forcing index/placement subsystem restarts.

sources.title: In the Matter of Knight Capital Americas LLC (SEC Order, Release No. 34-70694)
sources.mechanism: A deployment left dormant legacy code on one of eight servers and reused a flag that re-activated it; that server generated child orders without the stop condition that tracked parent-order fills, so an unbounded order loop ran for about 45 minutes.
sources.state_mapping: process_count (dim 0) as the count of runaway order-generating work items growing without a termination guard.
sources.caveats: Regulatory order focused on controls and financial loss; no engineering time-series of the runaway loop.
sources.verification: Fetched PDF; pypdf text confirms Release 34-70694, Oct 16 2013, the repurposed Power Peg flag, the eighth un-updated server, and millions of child orders in ~45 minutes.

sources.title: Details of the Cloudflare outage on July 2, 2019
sources.mechanism: A new rule contained a regular expression with catastrophic backtracking; it was pushed globally without staged rollout and drove CPU on every traffic-handling core to exhaustion, so the service stalled until the rule was withdrawn.
sources.state_mapping: heap_fraction (dim 1) used as a compute-saturation proxy climbing to 100% utilisation and stalling all processes (process_count effective throughput -> 0).
sources.caveats: CPU, not heap, is the literal saturated resource; mapping is by analogy. ~27-minute duration given but no utilisation curve.
sources.verification: Fetched page; confirmed title and the catastrophic-backtracking regex exhausting CPU globally, with a removed CPU safeguard.

sources.title: Summary of the AWS Service Event in the Northern Virginia (US-EAST-1) Region
sources.mechanism: Automated scaling triggered a large number of internal clients to surge connection activity, overwhelming the devices linking the internal and main networks; latency and errors made clients retry, which sustained the congestion, and degraded internal monitoring delayed diagnosis.
sources.state_mapping: process_count (dim 0) as surging/retrying connection work items; heap_fraction (dim 1) as device buffer pressure oscillating under the retry feedback loop.
sources.caveats: Describes the feedback qualitatively; no connection-rate time series published.
sources.verification: Fetched page; confirmed title, Dec 10 2021, and the connection-surge/retry congestion that also blinded monitoring.

sources.title: Apache Log4j Vulnerability Guidance
sources.mechanism: A crafted string written into a log triggers a directory lookup that loads and runs attacker-chosen remote code, giving control of the process with no authentication; the trigger looks like ordinary logging input.
sources.state_mapping: process_count (dim 0) rises as the compromised process spawns unexpected children; heap_fraction (dim 1) perturbed by injected workloads.
sources.caveats: Guidance page (archived, first issued Dec 2021); no incident-specific telemetry. The follow-on payload behaviour varies by campaign and is not characterised here.
sources.verification: Fetched page; confirmed title and that an attacker-controlled lookup in a logged string causes remote code execution without credentials, with widespread active exploitation.

sources.title: backdoor in upstream xz/liblzma leading to ssh server compromise
sources.mechanism: Malicious build-time code hidden in release tarballs (absent from the source repo) altered a compression library so a widely linked service's behaviour was covertly modified; the anomaly first surfaced only as higher CPU and added latency on logins.
sources.state_mapping: process_count (dim 0) / heap_fraction (dim 1) perturbed, plus a latency bias on an otherwise-normal service path (a slow, hidden offset until triggered).
sources.caveats: Discovery report, not a full forensic timeline; CISA alert (same date, CVE-2024-3094) corroborates. Distribution reach was limited before detection.
sources.verification: Fetched page; confirmed subject, author Andres Freund, Mar 29 2024, and the discovery via elevated SSH login CPU and ~0.5s added login latency.

sources.title: Understanding the Mirai Botnet
sources.mechanism: Self-propagating malware scanned for and logged into weakly secured networked devices, recruiting them into a botnet whose population doubled roughly every 75 minutes; the swarm then flooded a DNS provider with traffic, denying name resolution for many downstream sites.
sources.state_mapping: process_count (dim 0) as the growing count of scanning/attack work items; at a victim host, connection/heap pressure spikes under the flood.
sources.caveats: Peer-reviewed measurement study; infection counts are estimates from telescopes/scans, and the Dyn IP overlap (~71%) implies other hosts were also involved.
sources.verification: Fetched abstract page and the full PDF; pypdf text confirms ~65k devices in the first 20 hours, ~75-minute doubling time, 200k-300k steady state, and the Oct 21 2016 Dyn attack (~107k attacking IPs).

sources.title: Summary of the October 22, 2012 AWS Service Event in the US-East Region
sources.mechanism: A DNS update failed to reach some storage servers, so their reporting agents kept contacting a dead endpoint and slowly leaked memory; usage climbed until servers could no longer process requests, and monitoring never alarmed on the leak.
sources.state_mapping: heap_fraction (dim 1) rising monotonically toward exhaustion on each affected server, eventually stalling its process throughput.
sources.caveats: Describes the leak qualitatively; no per-server memory-growth curve. A separate aggressive throttling policy compounded recovery.
sources.verification: Fetched page; confirmed title and that a latent bug in a data-collection agent leaked memory after a stale DNS endpoint, until storage servers could no longer serve requests.

sources.title: Instapaper Outage Cause & Recovery
sources.mechanism: The main table's data file grew until it hit an inherited 2TB filesystem limit; new inserts then failed, and because every backup shared the same filesystem limit, recovery required rebuilding onto a new filesystem over many hours.
sources.state_mapping: disk_usage (dim 3) (and fs_file_count, dim 2) growing monotonically into a hard ceiling, past which writes fail (effective collapse).
sources.caveats: Engineering blog postmortem; the growth-to-limit is described, not plotted, and no monitoring existed to show the approach curve.
sources.verification: Fetched body text and HTML metadata via scrapling; confirmed author Brian Donohue, published 2017-02-14, and the 2TB ext3 file-size limit hit by the bookmarks table.

sources.title: W32.Stuxnet Dossier, Version 1.4
sources.publisher: Symantec Security Response (Falliere, O Murchu, Chien)
sources.mechanism: Malicious controller logic waited for a long benign period, then drove motor-drive output frequencies far outside normal bounds and back, while replaying previously recorded normal readings to the monitoring station so operators saw nominal values during the sabotage.
sources.dynamics_signature: actuator gain change or stuck actuator
sources.state_mapping: velocity (rotor speed forced to extreme set frequencies) and vibration (induced), while health/sensor feeds are masked by replayed normal values (stale or replayed sensor values).
sources.caveats: Covers the drive-frequency (rotor-speed) routine; the separate overpressure routine and plant-context analysis (Langner) are not from this source. Frequencies are code-derived, not measured plant telemetry.
sources.verification: Fetched PDF; pypdf text confirms Version 1.4 (February 2011), authors, the 1410 Hz / 2 Hz / 1064 Hz drive-frequency sequence versus a normal 807-1210 Hz band, and replay of prior frequencies to the monitoring system.

sources.title: Cyber-Attack Against Ukrainian Critical Infrastructure (IR-ALERT-H-16-056-01)
sources.mechanism: Using stolen credentials and remote-operation tools, attackers opened breakers at distribution substations to cut power, then corrupted device firmware, wiped operator workstations, and disrupted backup power to slow restoration.
sources.state_mapping: health (delivered-power/service availability) steps down as breakers open; link (comms quality) degraded by corrupted serial-to-ethernet devices; fault set.
sources.caveats: Does not mention the telephony denial-of-service on the call center; BlackEnergy's exact role is stated as unknown; no load time series.
sources.verification: Fetched page; confirmed title, alert code, the Dec 23 2015 incident, ~225,000 customers, remote breaker operation, KillDisk, and serial-to-ethernet firmware corruption.

sources.title: Compromise of U.S. Water Treatment Facility (AA21-042A)
sources.mechanism: An unauthorized actor reached the plant's control software and increased the setpoint for a chemical dose; a human operator noticed the changed value and corrected it before the change affected treatment or triggered an alarm.
sources.state_mapping: a controlled process variable (mapped to payload/health as the dosed-quantity analog) is stepped to an unsafe setpoint, then restored before downstream effect.
sources.caveats: Advisory gives no concentration figures (the ~100->11,100 ppm numbers come from press reporting, not this page), does not name the city, and states the remote-access tool and whether it was a targeted intrusion could not be confirmed.
sources.verification: Fetched page; confirmed title, advisory code, Feb 5 2021 incident, and that the actor raised the sodium hydroxide dosing setpoint via SCADA before an operator reversed it.

sources.title: Maroochy Water Breach (Campaign C0020)
sources.mechanism: Using insider knowledge and stolen radio equipment, an actor impersonated a control master to send false commands and altered parameters at pumping stations, while suppressing the alarms that would have reported the faults, causing large sewage releases.
sources.state_mapping: fault (pump functions altered) and link (spoofed radio control channel), with health degraded (spill) and alarm/health reporting suppressed.
sources.caveats: ATT&CK knowledge-base entry (2023) abstracting the 2000 incident; no raw telemetry, and it post-dates and summarizes earlier primary analyses.
sources.verification: Fetched page; confirmed campaign C0020, first/last seen Feb-Apr 2000, 800,000 liters of sewage, radio rogue-master commands, parameter changes, and alarm suppression.

sources.title: Attackers Deploy New ICS Attack Framework 'TRITON' and Cause Operational Disruption to Critical Infrastructure
sources.mechanism: Malware reached a safety-instrumented-system workstation and reprogrammed safety controllers; a validation mismatch instead drove some controllers into their fail-safe state, tripping an unplanned process shutdown and revealing the intrusion.
sources.state_mapping: fault set on the safety controller leading to a step shutdown: health/progress/velocity drop to zero when the safe state trips.
sources.caveats: Vendor threat report; the attacker's ultimate physical-damage intent is assessed with moderate confidence, and the shutdown was reportedly inadvertent. No process telemetry.
sources.verification: Fetched page; confirmed title, authors, Dec 14 2017, reprogramming of safety controllers over the proprietary protocol, and controllers entering a fail-safe shutdown after a validation check.

sources.title: Remote Exploitation of an Unaltered Passenger Vehicle
sources.mechanism: After remote access to the vehicle's head unit, researchers could place messages on the internal vehicle network to influence actuators; braking, engine, and steering effects were gated by the vehicle so they were reliable only at low speed.
sources.dynamics_signature: actuator gain change or stuck actuator
sources.state_mapping: velocity (engine cut), clearance (braking disabled so distance-keeping fails), and x/y (steering) perturbed by spoofed actuator commands.
sources.caveats: Abstracted here to dynamics only; the paper itself notes the physical-control work was limited and speed-gated. No continuous kinematic telemetry of a collision.
sources.verification: Fetched PDF; pypdf text confirms authors, Aug 10 2015, 2014 Jeep Cherokee target, and that physical effects (engine, braking, steering) were only reliably commandable at low speed.

sources.title: Assumptions Used in the Safety Assessment Process and the Effects of Multiple Alerts and Indications on Pilot Performance (ASR-19-01)
sources.mechanism: A single angle-of-attack sensor read a large erroneous offset; the automated trim function treated it as real and repeatedly drove nose-down, re-activating a few seconds after each manual correction, while related alerts from the same bad input added workload.
sources.state_mapping: a persistent sensor bias on the attitude input drives an actuator (pitch trim) in repeated steps: y (altitude/pitch) and velocity perturbed, fault set.
sources.caveats: Recommendation report derived from two ongoing foreign-led investigations; focuses on certification assumptions, not a complete probable-cause finding for either crash.
sources.verification: Fetched PDF; pypdf text confirms report date Sep 19 2019, accidents DCA19RA017/DCA19RA101, the ~20deg (Lion Air) and ~59deg (Ethiopian) AoA sensor offsets, and repeated automatic nose-down trim re-commanding 5 s after each pilot input.

sources.title: Collision Between Vehicle Controlled by Developmental Automated Driving System and Pedestrian, Tempe, Arizona, March 18, 2018 (NTSB/HAR-19/03)
sources.mechanism: The automated driving system detected the pedestrian 5.6 s out but kept reclassifying her (vehicle/unknown/bicycle), discarding the prior track each time so it never built a stable predicted path; a built-in 1-second braking suppression further delayed the response.
sources.state_mapping: clearance (closing distance) decreasing while the perception state keeps resetting; velocity unchanged during the 1 s suppression (delayed hazard), fault/health.
sources.caveats: Probable cause centers on operator distraction and safety culture; the perception-reset and suppression are system factors, and the published data are summary values, not raw sensor logs.
sources.verification: Fetched PDF; pypdf text confirms NTSB/HAR-19/03 adopted Nov 19 2019, first detection 5.6 s before impact, repeated reclassification that discarded tracking history, and a 1-second 'action suppression' before braking.

sources.title: Auxiliary Power Unit Battery Fire, Japan Airlines Boeing 787-8, JA829J, Boston, Massachusetts, January 7, 2013 (NTSB/AIR-14/01)
sources.mechanism: An internal short in one lithium-ion cell released heat that pushed it into thermal runaway; the heat propagated to neighboring cells in a self-accelerating chain, producing smoke and fire that design safeguards failed to contain.
sources.state_mapping: battery (state/temperature) and health degrade in an accelerating cell-to-cell cascade; vibration/thermal proxy and fault set.
sources.caveats: Investigation could not identify the exact short-initiating defect; describes the runaway qualitatively rather than as a cell-temperature time series.
sources.verification: Fetched PDF; pypdf text confirms NTSB/AIR-14/01 adopted Nov 21 2014 and the probable cause: an internal cell short leading to thermal runaway that cascaded to adjacent cells.

sources.title: Mars Climate Orbiter Mishap Investigation Board Phase I Report
sources.mechanism: A ground software file reported thruster impulse in pound-force-seconds while the navigation model assumed newton-seconds; the unit mismatch injected a small, consistent bias into the trajectory estimate that accumulated over months until the spacecraft entered too low and was lost.
sources.state_mapping: x, y (position/trajectory) drift from a constant scale-factor bias accumulating over time; progress toward the intended orbit diverges.
sources.caveats: Board report establishes the unit root cause and contributing process gaps; the trajectory error is reconstructed, not directly telemetered as a drift curve.
sources.verification: Fetched PDF; pypdf text confirms Nov 10 1999 and the root cause: a ground 'Small Forces' file produced thruster impulse in English units where the navigation software expected metric, so the trajectory ended ~170 km too low.

sources.title: Ariane 501 - Presentation of Inquiry Board report (N° 33–1996)
sources.mechanism: A software error in the inertial reference system caused both units to fail about 37 s after ignition; with guidance lost, the booster and main-engine nozzles swung to their extreme positions, the vehicle veered, and self-destruct triggered as designed.
sources.dynamics_signature: actuator gain change or stuck actuator
sources.state_mapping: fault (loss of guidance) followed by a step actuator command (full nozzle deflection) that drives x, y, and velocity off-course.
sources.caveats: This press-release page attributes the failure to an SRI software specification/design error but does not state the specific 64-bit-to-16-bit conversion overflow; that detail is in the full Inquiry Board report linked from the page, not on this page.
sources.verification: Fetched page; confirmed release N° 33-1996 dated 23 July 1996, the complete loss of guidance ~37 s after main-engine ignition from an inertial-reference software error, both reference systems failing, nozzles to extreme, and correct self-destruct.

sources.title: Global Navigation Satellite System Outage and Alterations Leading to Communication / Navigation / Surveillance Degradation (SIB 2022-02R4)
sources.mechanism: Spoofed satellite-navigation signals make receivers compute false position, navigation, and timing, which can trigger spurious terrain-warning pull-up alerts and corrupt time-dependent systems; jamming instead removes the signal outright, and some effects persist after the aircraft leaves the affected region.
sources.state_mapping: x, y, clearance biased by false position; link (navigation signal) dropping out in bursts; spurious hazard alerts map to fault/health perturbations.
sources.caveats: Advisory/information bulletin aggregating many occurrences across conflict regions; not a single incident and carries no numeric telemetry. A parallel maritime primary source exists (MARAD MSCI 2019-013, Eastern/Central Mediterranean GPS interference, https://www.maritime.dot.gov/msci/2019-013-easterncentral-mediterranean-sea-and-suez-canal-gps-interference, verified).
sources.verification: Fetched the attached PDF; pypdf text confirms SIB 2022-02R4 (issued 03 July 2026, correction 22 July 2026, revising 2022-02R3 of 05 July 2024) and the described spoofing effects: incorrect PNT, spurious TAWS PULL UP alerts, misleading time/clock/FMS, and effects persisting after leaving the affected area.

methods_reviewed.name: In-context identification of dynamical systems (enhanced Transformer)
methods_reviewed.citation: Rufolo, Piga, Maroni, Forgione, 'Enhanced Transformer architecture for in-context learning of dynamical systems', arXiv:2410.03291 (2024-10-04), https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.03291
methods_reviewed.applicability: Meta-trained model infers an unknown system from a short input/output context at test time and adds a probabilistic output head plus long-context patching - fits fast adaptation to a newly perturbed regime without retraining the small dynamics model.

methods_reviewed.name: Chronos (tokenized probabilistic time-series forecasting)
methods_reviewed.citation: Ansari et al., 'Chronos: Learning the Language of Time Series', arXiv:2403.07815 (2024-03-12), https://arxiv.org/abs/2403.07815
methods_reviewed.applicability: Quantizes series into tokens and forecasts a full predictive distribution, pretrained partly on synthetic data - gives calibrated probabilistic forecasts whose tails can serve as early constraint-violation (threshold-crossing) warnings.

methods_reviewed.name: Autocorrelated multi-step conformal prediction (AcMCP)
methods_reviewed.citation: Wang & Hyndman, 'Online conformal inference for multi-step time series forecasting', arXiv:2410.13115 (2024-10-17), https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.13115
methods_reviewed.applicability: Distribution-free multi-step prediction intervals that exploit error autocorrelation and keep coverage online - directly suited to issuing horizon-aware, calibrated warnings before a forecast state crosses a safety limit.

methods_reviewed.name: OMNI-EPIC (open-ended, code-generated environments)
methods_reviewed.citation: Faldor, Zhang, Cully, Clune, 'OMNI-EPIC: Open-endedness via Models of human Notions of Interestingness with Environments Programmed in Code', arXiv:2405.15568 (2024-05-24), https://arxiv.org/abs/2405.15568
methods_reviewed.applicability: Foundation models write code for new, learnable-yet-interesting tasks and tune difficulty to the agent - a POET/ACCEL-style way to auto-generate and evolve a curriculum of simulator perturbation scenarios that stress the dynamics model.

methods_reviewed.name: Dream-RSI (replay-simulator self-improvement)
methods_reviewed.citation: Zheng et al., 'Dream-RSI: Recursive Self-Improvement through Evolving Worlds', arXiv:2609.14858 (2026-09-14), https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.14858
methods_reviewed.applicability: Treats the history of past discoveries as a replay simulator to refine exploration policies cheaply off-policy before redeploying - analogous to using the learned world model itself as a cheap replay environment to improve forecasting/exploration between real rollouts.

unverified_candidates: Langner 'To Kill a Centrifuge' PDF (https://www.langner.com/wp-content/uploads/2017/03/to-kill-a-centrifuge.pdf) - the direct PDF 301-redirected to otbase.com and could not be fetched; Stuxnet is therefore sourced from the Symantec W32.Stuxnet Dossier instead.

NIOSH FACE report full8420.html (https://www.cdc.gov/niosh/face/in-house/full8420.html) and NIOSH 85-103 (https://www.cdc.gov/niosh/docs/85-103/default.html) both returned HTTP 404; an industrial-robot fatality source was consequently NOT included in the final 24. If a 25th physical source is wanted, the mechanism is corroborated by two verified NIOSH-authored pages: 'Working with robots: supervisor awareness can help prevent fatalities' (Collins & Etherton, Professional Safety 35(3):15-18, 1990-03-01, https://stacks.cdc.gov/view/cdc/205908) and MMWR 'Occupational Fatality Associated with a Robot -- Michigan' (https://www.cdc.gov/mmwr/preview/mmwrhtml/00000505.htm).
